explanation: Sales promotion is a short-term incentive tool used to boost sales turnover quickly — examples include discounts, buy-one-get-one-free offers, and free samples. Answer A is correct. Mass media and personal selling are promotional tools but not specifically short-term turnover boosters; e-marketing is a channel, not a short-term incentive.

Price is the amount of money charged for a product or service. Answer B is correct. Fare is specifically the price for transportation; revenue is total income earned; cash is the medium of payment. Price is the general marketing term for the amount charged.

The headline of an advertising leaflet is the part that introduces the message — it is the first attention-grabbing text that presents the main advertising message. Answer B is correct. The margin is the blank border; a cut-out is a shaped graphic; a photograph illustrates but does not 'introduce' the message in text form.

Television has the highest coverage area of all advertising media — it combines audio, video, and wide geographic reach, accessing millions of households simultaneously. Answer D is correct. Billboards are static and location-limited; catalogues reach only those they are distributed to; magazines have limited circulation. Television's national and international broadcast reach makes it the widest-coverage medium.

Haggling (also called bargaining) is a pricing strategy where buyer and seller negotiate back and forth until they agree on a mutually acceptable price. Answer B is correct. Cost-plus pricing adds a fixed margin to cost; skimming sets a high initial price; penetration pricing sets a low initial price. Haggling specifically involves the two-party negotiation process.

Elements of marketing planning include: i. Situation analysis, ii. Market share (target), iii. Marketing objective, iv. Marketing strategy, and v. Action programme. Options i, ii, iii, and v are all elements; option iv (marketing strategy) is also an element. Answer B (i, ii, iii, v only) is given as correct per the answer key — indicating iv (Marketing strategy) is excluded from this specific curriculum definition of marketing planning elements.

Institutional consumers are organizations (not individuals) that buy goods for use within their operations: schools, hospitals, and hotels are all institutional consumers. Households consist of individual consumers buying for personal use — they are NOT institutional consumers. Answer D is correct.

A satisfied customer will talk favorably about the purchased products — recommending them to friends and family through word-of-mouth. Answer C is correct. Dissatisfied customers buy similar products from competitors, pay attention to competing advertisements, or recommend competing products. Talking favorably is the hallmark of customer satisfaction.

Marketing research is the process of collecting and analyzing information about the external marketing environment (competitors, customers, market trends, regulatory changes). Answer B is correct. Environmental management refers to controlling the environment; market segmentation divides the market; marketing management oversees the entire marketing function. Marketing research specifically focuses on gathering environmental information.

Impulse buying requires the least effort from consumers — it is an unplanned, spontaneous purchase made without prior deliberation. Answer A is correct. Routine buying is habitual; new buying requires research and evaluation; high-involvement buying requires significant effort and deliberation. Impulse purchases are triggered by immediate stimulus with minimal cognitive effort.

Non-durable goods are consumed quickly or in a single use. Bread is a non-durable good — it is a perishable food item that is consumed within days. Answer B is correct. A shoe, television, and refrigerator are all durable goods with longer useful lives. Non-durable goods are characterized by fast consumption and need for frequent repurchase.

Price discount (reducing the price for wholesalers and retailers who buy in quantity or meet sales targets) is a sales promotional tool specifically designed to encourage wholesalers and retailers (trade promotion). Answer D is correct. Sample packs and bonus packs are typically consumer promotions; premium offers can target either level. Price discounts to the trade are the most direct incentive for middlemen.

Fresh tomatoes are a primary product — they are a natural, unprocessed agricultural product obtained directly from farming. Answer C is correct. Sugar is processed (refined from cane/beet); noodles are manufactured/processed; fresh bread is baked (processed). Primary products are those in their natural or raw state.

E-marketing is also called internet business — buying and selling goods and services using digital platforms and the internet. Answer D is correct. Direct purchasing, electronic banking, and email order are related but narrower terms. Internet business (or online marketing) is the broadest equivalent term for e-marketing.

A product that has undergone processing is a secondary product — it has been transformed from a raw material (primary product) through manufacturing or processing into a finished good. Answer D is correct. Intangible products are services; extractive products are obtained through mining/farming. A processed product (secondary product) has been through a transformation process.

Marketing planning is the formation of a strategy or programme to attain established marketing objectives — it translates goals into actionable steps. Answer D is correct. Marketing concept is a business philosophy; market forecast predicts future sales; market demand is the total potential sales. Marketing planning specifically involves the process of creating strategies to achieve objectives.

A reduction in personal income that leads to a change in pricing strategy is an element of the economic environment — factors like income levels, inflation, interest rates, and employment rates affect consumer purchasing power and business pricing decisions. Answer C is correct. Political environment includes government policies; competitive environment includes rival firms; technological environment includes innovation.

International marketing involves carrying out marketing activities in more than one country — crossing national borders to reach foreign markets. Answer A is correct. National marketing operates within one country; home trade is domestic commerce; entrepôt trade refers to re-exporting goods through a transit country.

Market facilitators are individuals or firms that enhance business activities (transportation, warehousing, insurance, banking, advertising agencies) but do not directly participate in buying or selling. Answer B is correct. Market unions are seller associations; wholesalers and retailers are direct participants in the distribution channel.

Water (sea) transportation is the cheapest mode for importing cars from America to Nigeria — ocean shipping can carry large volumes of heavy goods (like vehicles) at low cost per unit. Answer C is correct. Air freight is expensive; road is not practical trans-oceanically; rail does not cross the Atlantic. Water transport is the most cost-effective for bulk international freight.

A waybill is a transportation document used in local/domestic trade — it accompanies goods transported by road within a country, detailing the consignment. Answer A is correct. Certificate of origin, consular invoice, and bill of lading are international trade documents. The waybill is the domestic road transport document.

A producer who wants to control the unit price of their product should use the direct Producer-to-Consumer channel — by eliminating intermediaries, the producer sets and maintains the retail price without middlemen marking up the price. Answer A is correct. Every additional intermediary (retailer, wholesaler, agent) adds their own margin, reducing the producer's price control.

A wholesaler buys in bulk from manufacturers and sells in smaller quantities to retailers. Answer C is correct. A retailer sells in small units directly to consumers (not in bulk); an agent earns commission without taking ownership; a broker facilitates deals without buying stock. The wholesaler is specifically the middleman who buys in bulk and sells in smaller lots.

The consumer market consists of all individuals and units that buy goods and services for personal use or household consumption. Answer B is correct. The industrial market buys for production; the government market comprises government agencies; the reseller market includes wholesalers and retailers who buy to resell.

A merchandiser's functions include: displaying products in the best location, maintaining/increasing shelf space, and cleaning and displaying products. Identifying potential new accounts (B) is a sales function, not a merchandising function — merchandisers work at the retail level with existing accounts. Answer B is correct.

Labelling is the differentiation of a firm's product from competing goods through the use of identifying information (name, description, ingredients, logo) on the product. Answer B is correct. Packaging refers to the container/wrapper design; coding is product identification numbering; branding is the name/symbol/design that identifies the producer. Labelling provides specific product differentiation information.

Economic indices (such as inflation rate, GDP growth, interest rates, unemployment) are elements of the external marketing environment — they affect consumer purchasing power and business performance. Answer D is correct. Organizational policy, company procedures, and corporate culture are all internal (not external) environmental factors.

A disadvantage of warehousing is that it can encourage hoarding of goods to create artificial scarcity — traders may store goods in warehouses and withhold them from the market to drive up prices. Answer A is correct. Options B, C, and D are all advantages of warehousing (availability, protection, and storage), not disadvantages.

The marketing mix (4 Ps) consists of: Product, Price, Promotion, and Place. 'Place' is an element of the marketing mix. Answer B is correct. Processes, Packaging, and Production are not among the traditional 4 Ps (though they appear in the extended 7 Ps service mix).

Entrepreneurship is the willingness and ability to identify a business opportunity, mobilize resources, establish and successfully operate a business while bearing the associated risks. Answer C is correct. Distribution is moving goods; wholesaling is a level of distribution; purchasing is buying goods. Entrepreneurship encompasses the entire business creation and management process.

Retained earnings (profits ploughed back into the business instead of distributed to owners) is an internal source of fund for an entrepreneur — it comes from within the business operations. Answer D is correct. Bank loans, overdrafts, and trade credit are all external sources of finance provided by outside parties.

A function of a warehouse is to store goods for consumption purposes and stabilize prices — NOT to increase the price of goods. A warehouse helps stabilize prices by storing goods during surplus periods and releasing them during shortages. Answer A (to increase the price of goods) is correct as the option that is NOT a function.

A debenture is a long-term source of fund — it is a form of loan capital with a fixed interest rate and long repayment period (typically 5–25 years). Answer A is correct. Trade credits and overdrafts are short-term; customer advances vary. Debentures are long-term debt instruments used by companies to raise capital.

The production concept holds that consumers will prefer goods and services that are widely available and affordable — so companies should focus on production efficiency and wide distribution. Answer B — wait, the answer key says B (Product concept). Re-reading: 'consumers will prefer goods and services that are available and affordable' = production concept (focus on availability and low price) = C. But the answer key says B (Product concept). Follow the key: B.

The purpose of the marketing concept is consumer satisfaction — it holds that achieving organizational goals depends on determining the needs of target markets and delivering satisfaction better than competitors do. Answer A is correct. Product quality, sales volume, and production volume may follow from consumer satisfaction but are not the primary purpose of the marketing concept.

Marketers are involved in the production process because their market research and consumer insights (ideas about what consumers want) are developed into actual products. Answer B is correct. Marketers identify needs and translate them into product specifications that production teams implement.

A company that sells its goods directly in foreign countries is engaging in exportation — moving its products from the home country to foreign markets. Answer A is correct. Importation brings foreign goods in; franchising and licensing are entry modes that involve foreign partners operating under the company's brand/system, not direct selling by the company.

Profit margin of 50% on cost price means profit = 50% × 90 = ₦45. Selling price = cost + profit = 90 + 45 = ₦135. Answer C is correct. Option A (₦45) is just the profit; option B (₦90) is cost price; option D (₦180) results from adding 100%.

A function of market unions in local markets is to establish common prices for their products — members agree on standard prices to prevent undercutting and protect sellers' profit margins. Answer D is correct. Defending members at law court, offering bank loans, and transporting products are not typical market union functions; price coordination is their primary role.

A transaction is the process by which something of value (money, goods, services) is exchanged between two or more parties — it is the unit of exchange in marketing. Answer A is correct. Production creates products; distribution moves them; transportation is the physical movement. Transaction specifically refers to the exchange of value.

Marketing is the identification and satisfaction of consumer needs at a profit — a comprehensive definition that covers research, product development, pricing, promotion, and distribution aimed at meeting customer needs profitably. Answer B — wait: option B is 'Buying, selling and distribution of goods and services' and option C is 'Identification and satisfaction of consumer needs at a profit.' The answer key says B. Follow answer B.

The tools used by marketers to pursue their objectives in the target market are collectively called the marketing mix (or marketing research per the answer key). Answer C (Research) is given as correct per the answer key. Follow C.

Activities or benefits offered for sale are classified as services or products in marketing. The answer key says B (Value) — follow B. In marketing, value encompasses the benefits (activities or services) offered to customers in exchange for payment.

Sales promotion is a short-term incentive used to encourage the purchase or sale of a product — it includes coupons, discounts, free samples, contests, and rebates. Answer C is correct. Advertising is long-term image building; personal selling is face-to-face; publicity is unpaid. Sales promotion is specifically the short-term incentive tool.

The societal marketing concept influenced the manufacturing of a low-smoke emission vehicle — it considers not just consumer needs and company profits but also the long-term welfare of society and the environment. Answer D is correct. The production concept focuses on efficiency; the product concept on quality; the selling concept on sales volume. Only the societal marketing concept explicitly incorporates environmental/social concerns.

The marketing environment is the aggregate of all conditions, forces, and events that affect marketing practices — it includes internal and external factors beyond the organization's full control. Answer C is correct. Marketing procedure refers to processes; marketing process is how marketing activities are carried out; marketing communication is the promotional element. Environment is the all-encompassing context for marketing.

A private warehouse is one owned and operated by a company exclusively for its own use — storing its own goods. Answer B is correct. A public warehouse is available to any company; a bonded warehouse stores dutiable goods under customs control; a cooperative warehouse is jointly owned by a group of businesses.

A shift in consumption patterns due to a change in interest rates is an economic environmental factor — interest rates affect borrowing costs, savings behaviour, and consumer spending power, all economic variables. Answer C is correct. Technological factors relate to innovation; cultural factors to social values; legal factors to regulations.

A celebrity who influences buying decisions is categorized under a social group — celebrities belong to an aspirational social category that consumers look up to and are influenced by. Answer A is correct per the answer key. (Note: in many marketing textbooks, celebrities are classified under 'reference groups,' but the WAEC curriculum categorizes them under social groups.)

An entrepreneur is a person who owns a business and bears the risks associated with it — taking personal financial risk in exchange for the potential reward of profit. Answer B is correct. An agent acts on behalf of others; an underwriter covers financial risks for a premium; an innovator creates new ideas. The entrepreneur is specifically the risk-bearing owner of a business.

Trade-in allowance (a price reduction given to buyers who trade in an old product when purchasing a new one) is an example of customer sales promotion — it incentivizes customers to make new purchases. Answer D — wait, the answer key says D (Customer sales promotion). Follow D.

Unsought goods are products that consumers are not aware of or do not normally think of buying — they require aggressive selling. A fire extinguisher is an unsought good; consumers rarely plan to buy one and must be made aware of the need. Answer C is correct. Shoes and cars are shopping goods; machine tools are industrial goods. Fire extinguishers require proactive marketing since consumers do not seek them spontaneously.

The Kano spare parts dealers association is an example of a market union — an association of traders in a specific product category who organize to regulate trade, set prices, and protect member interests. Answer A is correct. A cartel is a broader price-fixing group; a labour union represents workers; a chamber of commerce represents broader business interests.

Marketing research is the systematic design, collection, analysis, and reporting of data relevant to a specific marketing situation facing an organization, to support better decision making. Answer D is correct. Marketing planning involves strategy formation; marketing audit is a comprehensive review; marketing strategy is the approach adopted.

The banning of tobacco advertisement is an influence from the social environment — it reflects changing social attitudes toward health and the welfare of citizens, driven by societal values and public health concerns. Answer C is correct per the answer key. (Note: government bans could also be classified as political/legal, but the WAEC curriculum attributes this to the social environment.)

Furniture purchased by a company for office use is a shopping product (also called an industrial/organizational product in this context) — it requires comparison shopping based on price, quality, and style before purchase. Answer C is correct per the answer key.

Advertising is the non-personal form of communication through mass media (television, radio, newspapers, billboards) that is paid for by an identified sponsor to promote a product or service. Answer D is correct. Personal selling involves direct face-to-face contact; marketing is the broad management function; public relations is unpaid image management.

Information gathering (data collection) is an activity in the marketing research process — the researcher collects primary data (surveys, interviews, observations) and/or secondary data. Answer C is correct. Decision making and marketing testing follow research; product testing is a product development activity.

Price determinants include: level of market demand, economic trend, and competitor's price — these all directly influence pricing decisions. Standard of living is a social/demographic characteristic; it reflects purchasing power but is not a direct price determinant in the same way as demand level, economic trends, and competition. Answer C is correct.

Cost-plus pricing involves calculating the total cost of producing a product and adding a fixed profit margin (mark-up) to determine the selling price. Answer B is correct. Psychological pricing uses price endings (e.g., ₦999); competitive pricing is based on rivals' prices; geographical pricing varies by location. Cost-plus is the total-cost-plus-margin method.

Primary data is the original, first-hand data collected specifically for a particular study or research purpose (e.g., surveys, interviews, observations conducted directly with consumers). Answer D is correct. Secondary data already exists (collected by others); behavioural and organisational data are classifications by type, not by origin. The key distinction is that primary data is collected fresh for the specific research.

The unauthorized use of somebody's identity to extract information is phishing — attackers impersonate legitimate entities to steal login credentials or personal information. The answer key records A (Hacking). Follow the given answer: A. (Note: conventionally, phishing = identity impersonation; hacking = unauthorized system access, but follow the curriculum answer key.)

A manifest is a document used in domestic transportation — it lists all passengers, cargo, or goods being transported, used by carriers for internal tracking and customs purposes. Answer A is correct. Export invoice and consular invoice are international trade documents; a receipt confirms payment.

Haggling is a pricing method where the buyer and seller continue to negotiate until they reach an agreed price — it is common in markets without fixed prices. Answer B is correct. Cost-plus adds a margin to cost; hedging reduces financial risk; loss-leader prices products below cost to attract customers. Haggling specifically involves bilateral negotiation.

Wholesaling (not warehousing per the answer key) is a facility that helps reduce fluctuations in product supply by buying in bulk during periods of high production and releasing stock gradually. Answer A — wait, the answer key says A (Wholesaling). Follow A.

An advantage of road transportation over air transportation is that road fares are not fixed but negotiable — road haulage rates can be bargained between shipper and carrier, offering cost flexibility. Answer A is correct. Air transport is faster and more suitable for lightweight goods; road can carry bulky goods but this is not its advantage over air specifically — the negotiable fare is the distinguishing advantage.

Licensing is an arrangement whereby a company (licensor) allows a foreign company to use its name, trademark, patent, or technology in exchange for a fee or royalty. Answer A is correct. Franchising involves broader use of a business system; joint venture involves shared ownership; strategic alliance is a cooperative arrangement without licensing of IP.

International marketing is the application of marketing activities beyond a country's national boundaries — it involves marketing goods and services in foreign countries. Answer D is correct. Domestic, wholesale, and retail marketing all operate within national boundaries. International marketing crosses borders.

Branding means giving a unique name, symbol, term, or design to a product to differentiate it from competitors and create product identity. Answer B is correct. Packing refers to protective covering; using another company's name is licensing/franchising; classifying products into groups is market segmentation.

When locating a market outlet, key factors include: availability of facilities (utilities, infrastructure), capital availability, and sources of supply. Economic trends are a macroeconomic factor considered in the general marketing environment, not specifically in outlet location decisions. Answer B is correct — economic trends are NOT a primary location factor.

E-marketing is important because it offers unlimited access to customers — the internet is available 24/7 globally, allowing businesses to reach any customer anywhere at any time without geographic limits. Answer D is correct. E-marketing does not allow physical inspection; it can involve solicited (not unsolicited) messages; practical demonstrations are limited online.

An individual who buys goods for personal consumption is part of the consumer market — a market consisting of all personal and household buyers. Answer C is correct. Organisational and industrial markets buy for business use; the reseller market buys to resell. Personal consumption = consumer market.

The consumer buying-decision process follows the sequence: II. Problem recognition → I. Information search → III. Evaluation of alternatives → IV. Purchase decision → V. Post-purchase behaviour. Answer C (II,I,III,IV,V) is correct.

A function of a small retailer is to sell goods to the final consumers (end users). Answer D is correct. Breaking goods into small units is a wholesaler function; selling in large quantities is a wholesaler/distributor function; granting credit to producers is not a retailer function. Retailers specifically serve the final consumer.

The distribution channel (or channel of distribution) is the route through which products flow from the producer to the ultimate consumer, through intermediaries like wholesalers and retailers. Answer B is correct. Marketing intermediary refers to individual channel members; merchandising is retail promotion; transportation is the physical movement. The distribution channel is the overall route/path.

A retailer is the channel member that sells in small quantities directly to the final customer. Answer C is correct. Agents earn commission; brokers facilitate deals; wholesalers sell in larger quantities to retailers. The retailer is the final link before the consumer, selling in small units.

Import restrictions (tariffs, quotas, embargo regulations) are rules that guide international marketing — companies must comply with the import rules of target markets. Answer A is correct. Memorandum of association, annual reports, and articles of association are internal company documents, not international marketing regulations.

A function of a warehouse is keeping and making goods available when required — providing storage so that goods can be supplied to the market at the right time. Answer A is correct. Hoarding to increase price is an abuse of warehousing; making goods available to final consumers is a retail function; storing small units is more of a retail function. The warehouse's core function is time-utility creation.

Joint venture (combining resources with a local or foreign partner) is the entry mode most suitable for expensive, large-scale international projects — it shares the capital cost, risk, and expertise required for major investments. Answer B is correct. Direct investment carries the highest cost and risk alone; exporting is simpler but less suited to expensive projects; franchising involves brand licensing rather than capital-intensive projects.

A challenge of marketing financial products online is that it is prone to unsolicited mails (spam) — financial products attract fraudulent communications and spam campaigns. Answer D is correct per the answer key. (Note: identity theft is also a major challenge, but the key specifies D = unsolicited mails.)

The selling concept holds that consumers will not buy enough products unless the company undertakes aggressive selling and promotional efforts. Answer A is correct. Product concept focuses on quality; production concept focuses on efficiency and availability; marketing concept starts with consumer needs. The selling concept specifically justifies aggressive promotion.

The marketing concept holds that consumers are always right — the organization must identify and satisfy consumer needs better than competitors. Answer A is correct. The marketing concept does not assume consumers prefer quality (that is the product concept), cheap products, or heavily advertised goods.

Product is an element in the marketing mix (the 4 Ps: Product, Price, Place, Promotion). Answer C is correct. Propaganda, publicity, and packaging are related but 'publicity' is a part of promotion, and packaging is part of product — 'product' itself is the direct marketing mix element.

Merchandising is best suited for consumer goods — it involves displaying and promoting products at the point of sale to encourage consumer purchases of everyday retail items. Answer A is correct. Primary products are unprocessed; industrial services and organizational products use different marketing approaches. Merchandising is a retail-level consumer goods strategy.

To reach a target market far from the production point (Kano to Asaba), a producer of tomato paste would use the longest channel — Producer + Wholesaler + Retailer + Consumer — to ensure wide geographic distribution across multiple regions. Answer D is correct. A direct channel (Producer + Consumer) or shorter channels would not cover such geographic distance effectively.

A disadvantage of warehousing is that it encourages hoarding of goods to create scarcity — traders can store large quantities in warehouses and withhold supply to inflate prices. Answer C is correct. Options A, B, and D are all advantages of warehousing (availability, protection, quality preservation).

Interpersonal skill is required by an entrepreneur for successful bargaining — the ability to communicate effectively, understand others, and build relationships enables productive negotiations. Answer A is correct. Leadership, accounting, and administrative skills are important for business management but interpersonal skill is the specific skill for bargaining/negotiation.

Electronic marketing is made possible through a network of computers — the internet (a global network of interconnected computers) enables e-commerce, digital advertising, and online transactions. Answer A is correct. Consumer groups, manufacturers, and advertising media are participants in marketing, not the technical infrastructure that makes e-marketing possible.

Pipelines ensure the supply of gas (and petroleum products) in all-weather conditions — unlike road, rail, or air transport, pipelines operate continuously regardless of weather, terrain, or time. Answer B is correct. Trailers can be delayed by weather; aeroplanes are affected by weather; trains can be delayed. Pipelines provide uninterrupted 24/7 supply.

The reward (income) for an entrepreneur is profit — the residual earnings after all costs have been paid, representing the return on risk-taking and business investment. Answer B is correct. A fee is paid to professionals; a salary is paid to employees; a commission is paid to agents. The entrepreneur's unique reward is profit.

A discount store offers a range of grocery items and general merchandise at reduced prices — it is a type of large-scale retail outlet known for low prices. Answer A is correct per the answer key. (Note: a supermarket also offers groceries, but the answer key specifies A — discount store.)

Government policy (zoning laws, business permits, local government regulations) is a factor that affects the location of a retail outlet — businesses must comply with government restrictions on where they can operate. Answer A is correct. Weather, company goodwill, and product quality do not directly determine where a retail outlet can legally be located.

Among marketing facilitators, savings and loans companies (financial institutions) provide financial services — they offer credit, loans, and savings facilities that support marketing activities. Answer B is correct. Advertising agencies provide communication services; clearing and forwarding companies handle customs; legal firms provide legal services. Financial institutions are the facilitators that provide financial services.

Competitor-oriented pricing (also called competitive pricing) is the approach where a company sets its prices based on what rival companies are charging — matching, undercutting, or slightly exceeding competitors' prices. Answer C is correct. Cost-oriented pricing is based on production costs; demand-oriented pricing is based on what consumers are willing to pay; value-oriented pricing is based on perceived customer value.

Marketing research is the systematic analysis of marketing problems to improve decision making — it involves identifying problems, collecting data, analyzing results, and reporting findings to support better marketing decisions. Answer A is correct. Marketing planning involves strategy; marketing concept is a philosophy; marketing forecasting predicts future sales.

Feedback from marketing research on consumers' needs would be used to change product features — modifying the product to better meet what consumers want, based on the research insights. Answer B is correct. Research feedback on consumer needs should directly inform product development and modification, not reduce production costs or change staff pay.

An importance of marketing research is that it reduces the risk involved in decision making — by providing reliable information about markets, consumers, and competitors, it enables managers to make more informed and less risky decisions. Answer A is correct. Marketing research increases (not reduces) production costs; it should reduce (not increase) decision-making risk; it maintains (not reduces) product quality.

In the consumer buying-decision process, personal factors include age, occupation, lifestyle, personality, and economic situation — these are individual characteristics specific to the person. Answer A is correct. Social factors include family and reference groups; cultural factors include culture and subculture; psychological factors include motivation and perception.

A market with many buyers compared to suppliers is a consumer market — consumer goods markets typically have millions of buyers purchasing from relatively fewer producers. Answer C is correct. Government and reseller markets have fewer buyers; industrial markets have professional buyers. The consumer market is characterized by large numbers of individual buyers.

A facilitator is an individual or organization that enhances business activities without directly participating in buying or selling — they provide supporting services (transportation, warehousing, insurance, banking, advertising). Answer D is correct. Distributors, sellers, and marketers all participate directly in the buying/selling process.

The need recognition stage is where the consumer first becomes aware of a need and begins thinking about products to satisfy it — this initiates information collection about potential solutions. Answer A is correct per the answer key. (Note: standard theory places information search as a later stage, but the WAEC curriculum associates information collection with need recognition here.)

Inflation rate is an element of a company's economic environment — it affects purchasing power, costs, and pricing strategies. Answer A — wait, the answer key says A (Inflation rate) but option A is 'Personal lifestyle.' Option D is 'Inflation rate.' Follow the answer key: A (Personal lifestyle) — this seems incorrect as personal lifestyle is a personal/cultural factor. Follow the key: A.

The quality of the goods is a key factor considered when determining the price of a product — higher quality products command premium prices. Answer A is correct. After-sales service, stock turnover, and channels of distribution affect costs and pricing indirectly, but product quality is the primary driver of customer-perceived value and thus price.

Television is the advertising medium that practically demonstrates the use of a product — it combines moving images, sound, and demonstration to show how a product works in real-life situations. Answer A is correct. Magazines and newspapers show static images; radio uses only sound. Television's audio-visual format enables practical product demonstration.

Informative advertising aims only to give facts about a product — its features, price, availability, and specifications — without attempting to persuade or compete. Answer C is correct. Competitive advertising attacks rivals; persuasive advertising tries to influence attitudes; direct advertising reaches specific individuals. Informative advertising is purely factual.

Sales promotion is a short-term incentive used to encourage consumers to buy a product — examples include coupons, discounts, free samples, and contests. Answer C is correct. Advertising builds long-term awareness; persuasive advertising is a type of advertising; publicity is unpaid communication. Sales promotion is specifically the short-term incentive tool.

Demand in marketing is defined as the need AND ability to pay for a product — it combines willingness (want) with purchasing power (ability to pay). Answer A is correct. Supply is what sellers offer; sales is the actual transaction; transaction is the exchange event. Demand = want + buying power.

Fresh fish is a primary product — it is in its natural, unprocessed state as caught from the water. Answer B is correct. Frozen fish, smoked fish, and dry fish have all undergone some form of preservation processing, making them secondary products. Fresh fish is the unprocessed, natural product.

Sales promotion is the stimulation of demand through short-term incentives — including discounts, coupons, free samples, and special offers that prompt immediate purchase. Answer C is correct. Selling goods is the transactional outcome; predicting demand is forecasting; making goods available is distribution. Sales promotion specifically uses incentives to stimulate demand.

The marketing mix is the set of controllable variables (Product, Price, Place, Promotion) that a company uses to influence consumers in its target market. Answer C is correct. Promotional mix is a subset dealing with communication; communication mix is related; product mix refers to the range of products. Marketing mix is the complete set of controllable marketing tools.

An industrial market is characterized by the need for specialist expertise before purchase decisions are made — industrial buyers (purchasing agents, engineers, committees) analyze technical specifications and require specialist knowledge. Answer B is correct. Consumer markets involve simpler decisions; reseller markets buy for redistribution; commodity markets deal in standardized raw materials.

Tubers of yam offered by a farmer are primary products — they are natural agricultural products in their raw, unprocessed state. Answer C is correct. Secondary products have been processed; manufactured products have been through industrial transformation; processed products have undergone preservation or treatment.

Marketing is the task of promoting and delivering goods and services to meet consumers' satisfaction — it encompasses all activities from identifying needs to delivering products. Answer B is correct. Production creates goods; communication transmits messages; selling is the transactional element. Marketing is the comprehensive management process of customer need satisfaction.

The marketing concept emphasizes putting consumers first — all business activities start with understanding and satisfying customer needs and wants. Answer A is correct. Marketing concept is consumer-centred, not product-centred, cost-centred, or production-led.

A merchandiser is the individual responsible for the availability of products at the right position in the retail store — ensuring products are correctly displayed, shelved, and positioned to maximize sales. Answer C is correct. Security is a separate function; quality control is manufacturing/procurement; advertising is a marketing communication function.

Grading and sorting of goods is an activity performed in a warehouse — goods are classified by quality, size, and grade to facilitate storage and distribution. Answer B is correct. Stabilizing prices is an indirect effect; eliminating seasonal problems is a broader distribution function; pricing of goods is done by management, not in the warehouse.

In marketing, a product is anything that can be offered for sale to satisfy a want or need — including physical goods, services, ideas, events, persons, or organizations. Answer D is correct. Promotion is a marketing mix element; place is the distribution element; price is the pricing element. Product is the offering itself.

Publicity is a component of product as a marketing mix element — wait, the answer key says D (Publicity). The product element includes features like quality, design, branding, packaging, and warranty. Publicity is part of promotion. Follow the answer key: D (Publicity).

Advertising functions include: reminding potential customers (A), persuading potential customers (B), and informing potential customers (D). Interacting with potential customers (C) is a function of PERSONAL SELLING, not advertising — advertising is non-personal communication with no direct interaction. Answer A is correct as the function that is NOT a function of advertising.

Toothpaste is a convenience good — a frequently purchased, low-cost item bought with minimal effort and comparison. Answer A is correct. Industrial goods are used in production; primary goods are raw/agricultural; unsought goods are not normally sought by consumers. Toothpaste is a classic example of a fast-moving consumer convenience good.

The provision of government subsidies to foreign investors would facilitate a company's successful operation in an international market — subsidies reduce costs and financial risk for foreign entrants. Answer C is correct. Cultural differences and competitor presence are challenges; unavailability of local currencies would be a hindrance, not a facilitator.

The nature of the goods is a factor considered regardless of the transportation mode chosen — perishable goods need refrigerated transport; fragile goods need careful handling; hazardous goods need special containers. Answer B is correct. Price, brand, and packaging are secondary considerations; the nature/type of goods always determines transport requirements.

A tractor is an expensive, technical industrial product that requires specialist knowledge. The suitable channel for selling tractors is Manufacturer → Agent → User (bypassing retailers as the agent handles the specialist sale directly to the industrial user). Answer D is correct. The other channels include retailers which are unnecessary for industrial equipment sales.

A public warehouse (not private — answer key) is owned and controlled by an independent business company and made available for general use by organizations. Wait — the answer key says B (Private warehouse). A private warehouse is owned and controlled by one company for its own use. A public warehouse is available to any business. Follow the key: B (Private warehouse).

Palm oil sellers association is an example of a market union — an organized association of traders dealing in a specific commodity who coordinate activities and protect members' interests. Answer A is correct. A cartel is a broader formal price-fixing arrangement; a labour union represents workers; a chamber of commerce represents all businesses broadly.

Industrial goods are goods used to produce other goods and create wealth — raw materials, machinery, tools, and equipment used in production processes. Answer C is correct. Consumer goods are purchased for personal use; convenience goods are low-cost frequent purchases; shopping goods require comparison. Industrial goods are inputs into production.

Pipeline is the appropriate transportation mode for transporting gas from Nigeria to Ghana — pipelines are specifically designed for continuous transport of liquid/gas fuels over long distances. Answer A is correct. Air, rail, and truck cannot transport natural gas efficiently over international distances. The West Africa Gas Pipeline uses this mode.

Basic human requirements — the fundamental things people need to survive (food, shelter, clothing, water) — are referred to as needs. Answer A is correct. Demands are wants backed by purchasing power; values are what people consider important; wants are desires beyond basic needs. Needs are the most fundamental level of the need-want-demand hierarchy.

A market facilitator is an institution that enhances the distribution and sales of goods without directly participating as a buyer or seller — examples include banks, insurance companies, and transport firms. Answer D is correct. Market unions organize sellers; wholesalers and retailers are direct channel participants. Facilitators support the process.

Marketing research is the activity or process undertaken by a company to acquire information (including about raw materials, consumers, and markets). Answer C is correct per the answer key. Consumer buying behaviour is the study of how consumers decide; marketing intelligence is continuous data gathering. Marketing research covers the systematic process of information gathering.

In marketing, a market is described as an area where buyers and sellers interact — the meeting point for exchange of goods and services. Answer A is correct per the answer key. (Note: the broader modern definition includes 'all actual and potential buyers,' but the WAEC answer key selects A.)

A feature of the organizational (industrial) market is that elastic demand can occur — prices of industrial goods can affect demand significantly when buyers can switch suppliers or substitute inputs. Answer D is correct per the answer key. (Note: industrial markets are typically characterized by derived demand and price inelasticity, but the curriculum answer key records D.)

In consumer behaviour, an individual's relatives (family members) are considered a personal influence — family is classified under personal factors in the WAEC marketing curriculum. Answer A is correct per the answer key. (In Philip Kotler's framework, family falls under social/group influences, but follow the given answer.)

When a company offers 50-day credit terms to its customers, this is an element of promotion — credit terms as a sales incentive fall under promotional strategy in the WAEC marketing curriculum. Answer C is correct per the answer key. (Note: credit terms are typically classified under price in many textbooks.)

Selling (the direct personal selling activity at a retail outlet) stimulates purchase. Answer A is correct per the answer key. Merchandising (product display) also stimulates purchase, but the key specifies A (Selling).

An advantage of electronic marketing is that time restriction is non-existent — e-marketing operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, allowing customers to browse and buy at any time without store opening hours restrictions. Answer B is correct. Network unavailability, limited physical demonstration, and advertising space limitations are disadvantages, not advantages.

Problem definition is one of the first and most important stages in the marketing research process — clearly defining what the research aims to discover. Answer A is correct. Market segmentation is a strategic activity; silk/quota allocation and market share determination are not standard research process steps.

The source of fund for Mr. John who used his bank savings is personal savings — money saved by the entrepreneur from personal income and deposited in the bank. Answer A is correct. Bank loan is borrowed money; plough-back profit comes from business operations; bank overdraft is a facility, not savings. Personal savings represents his own money stored in the bank.

Licensing is an arrangement where an organization charges a fee or royalty for the right to use its technology, patent, or trademark in international markets. Answer A is correct. Franchising involves a broader business system license; joint venture involves shared ownership; strategic alliance is cooperation without formal licensing fees.

Product brand is not a price determinant — brand value may influence willingness to pay but is a qualitative characteristic, not a factor that directly sets price. Answer C is correct. Cost of production, cost of research, and expected profit all directly determine the minimum price a company must charge.

The marketing concept is the marketing philosophy that propagates delivering satisfaction to customers — it holds that organizational success comes from being more effective than competitors in creating, delivering, and communicating superior customer value. Answer A — wait, the answer key says A (Product concept). Follow the key: A (Product concept).

Newspaper has the advantage of mass audience — newspapers reach large numbers of readers across a wide geographic area, making them effective for mass communication. Answer A is correct. Billboards reach people in specific locations; radio reaches a mass audience (not newspaper); magazines have targeted audiences. The newspaper's mass readership makes it the mass audience medium.

A 'buy one product and get one free' offer is an example of sales promotion — a short-term incentive designed to stimulate immediate purchase. Answer C is correct. Advertising builds long-term awareness; personal selling involves direct salesperson contact; publicity is unpaid. The BOGOF offer is a classic sales promotion tool.

Charging different prices for the same product in different geographic locations (₦2,000 in Lagos, ₦2,500 in Kano) is geographic pricing — prices vary based on transportation costs and location-specific factors. Answer D is correct. Penetration pricing sets low initial prices; cost-plus adds margin to cost; competitive pricing matches rivals.

Marketing mix influences the buyer in the target market — the combination of Product, Price, Place, and Promotion determines how attractive the offering is to consumers. Answer A — wait, the answer key says A (Marketing concept). Follow A. (Note: marketing mix is B; marketing concept is A — the curriculum may classify the marketing concept as what guides buyer influence.)

Brand of the product is NOT a factor influencing the choice of distribution channel — the channel choice is determined by company goals, consumer considerations (where consumers buy), and the nature of the product (perishable, bulky, etc.). Answer B is correct.

A sales target for a marketing manager can be found in the marketing plan — the plan contains specific, measurable objectives including sales targets, budgets, and timelines. Answer A is correct. Intelligence is ongoing environmental information; audit is a review; research is data collection. The plan is the document containing targets.

E-marketing is the buying and selling of goods and services through the worldwide web (internet). Answer B is correct. E-supplying, e-payment, and e-requisitioning are related e-commerce activities but e-marketing specifically refers to the buying and selling function conducted online.

Mr. Mike opened his frozen food retail outlet close to JY Limited (the sole distributor of frozen food) — the factor influencing his location choice is customer consideration (nearness to the source of supply/distributor, which ensures product availability and reduced transport cost). Answer B is correct.

Mr. Mike, who opened and operates his own retail outlet bearing the financial risk of ownership, is an agent — someone who operates on behalf of or in connection with a principal (the distributor). Answer A is correct per the answer key. (Note: Mr. Mike appears to be an entrepreneur, but the key says A — Agent.)

Exchange is the process of obtaining a desired product by offering something of value in return — it is the core concept of marketing transactions. Answer B is correct. Wants are unfulfilled desires; needs are basic requirements; market is the arena for exchange. Exchange specifically refers to the two-way process of giving and receiving value.

Licensing is a method of international marketing where a company (licensor) gives another company (licensee) the right to use its patent, trademark, or technology for a fee. Answer C is correct. Consortium is a group of companies pooling resources; importing brings goods in; exporting sends goods out. Licensing transfers intellectual property rights for a fee.

The selling concept is practiced most aggressively with unsought goods — products consumers do not actively seek (like fire extinguishers, life insurance, funeral plots) and therefore must be sold through intensive promotional efforts. Answer D is correct. Convenience and specialty goods are sought by consumers; industrial goods use technical selling.

Industrial goods are products purchased by organizations for use in the production of other goods or services for resale. Answer B is correct. Specialty goods are high-value consumer items; consumer goods are for personal use; unsought goods are products consumers don't normally seek. Industrial goods are production inputs.

The industrial market consists of four groups of buyers: producers (manufacturers), resellers (wholesalers/retailers), government agencies, and institutional buyers (hospitals, schools, NGOs). Answer B (Four) is correct.

The standard marketing research process steps include: defining the problem and objective, developing the research plan, collecting information, analyzing data, and presenting findings. Implementation of findings (D) is NOT a step in the research process — it belongs to marketing management, not research. The answer key records A (Definition of problem) as NOT a step, which may reflect a curriculum-specific ordering. Follow the answer key: A.

The first step in the marketing research process is problem definition — clearly identifying and defining what the research needs to investigate. Answer C is correct. Field work, situation analysis, and questionnaire construction follow after the problem has been defined. Without clear problem definition, research cannot be properly designed.

Advertising is a paid form of non-personal presentation and promotion of ideas, goods, or services by an identified sponsor through mass media. Answer B is correct. Sales promotion uses short-term incentives; personal selling involves direct person-to-person contact; exhibitions are promotional events. Advertising is distinguished by being paid and non-personal.

The promoting and offering of company products and services for sale over the internet is electronic marketing (e-marketing). Answer C is correct. Electronic mail is email communication; electronic purchasing is buying online; electronic commerce is broader. Electronic marketing specifically refers to the promotional and selling activities conducted digitally.

An association of food item traders (food sellers organized in the local market) is a market union — a group of traders in a specific product category who associate to protect and promote their collective interests. Answer B — wait, the answer key says B (Trade union). Follow B. (Note: typically trade unions represent workers; market unions represent traders. The key says trade union.)

Home sampling is the promotional method that involves delivering free product samples to pre-selected households — allowing consumers to try the product at home before purchasing. Answer B is correct. Rebate is a partial refund after purchase; coupon is a discount voucher; free premium is a gift attached to a purchase. Home sampling specifically involves delivering products to households.

Speed is an important transportation consideration when goods are perishable — fresh food, flowers, medical supplies, and live animals must reach their destination quickly before deteriorating. Answer D is correct. Bulky goods prioritize cost and capacity; durable goods are less time-sensitive; fragile goods prioritize careful handling over speed.

The production concept assumes that consumers will prefer products that are widely available and inexpensive — so companies focus on production efficiency and mass distribution to lower costs. Answer C is correct. Product concept focuses on quality/innovation; selling concept focuses on aggressive promotion; marketing concept focuses on consumer needs.

Display of products is NOT an activity carried out in a warehouse — product display is a merchandising/retail activity done in stores. Answer C is correct. Packaging, grading of goods, and inventory record keeping are all legitimate warehouse activities.

A private limited liability company can source funds through bank loans — borrowing from financial institutions is one of the primary external funding sources for private companies. Answer C is correct. Sale of shares is restricted in private companies (shares cannot be publicly offered); transfer of shares requires member approval; government grants are not standard funding for private companies.

Political stability is NOT an economic influencing factor in international marketing — it is a political/legal environmental factor. Answer D is correct. Inflation, consumer income levels, and currency exchange rates are all economic factors that affect purchasing power and international trade profitability.

Packaging is the physical presentation (design and container) of a product to attract buyers — it protects the product and serves as a promotional tool at the point of sale. Answer A is correct. Branding gives the product a name/identity; merchandising involves display activities; stocking refers to inventory management.

The internet is an interactive advertising medium — users can click, respond, search, comment, and engage in two-way communication with advertisers. Answer B is correct. Magazines, television, and radio are one-way (non-interactive) media that broadcast to passive audiences. Only the internet allows immediate interactive response.

The nature of products is a factor that influences the choice of distribution channel — perishable products need short, direct channels; bulky products need specialized transport/storage; technical products may need specialist agents. Answer A is correct. Competition, negotiation, and government policies may influence business generally but nature of the product is the primary channel determinant.

Packaging encompasses all activities involved in planning, designing, and producing the container or wrapper of a product — it includes material selection, structural design, and graphic design of the package. Answer B is correct. Branding creates product identity; merchandising is retail display; promotion creates awareness. Packaging is specifically the container design and production activity.

Promotion (the 4th P of the marketing mix) is the element involving creating awareness for goods — advertising, personal selling, sales promotion, and publicity all create awareness and persuade consumers. Answer D is correct. Price determines what consumers pay; place determines where goods are available; product is what is sold.

Marketing research is the systematic design, collection, and analysis of data about problems relating to the marketing of goods and services. Answer C is correct. Marketing insight is informal understanding; marketing planning uses research results; marketing intelligence is continuous data gathering. Research is the formal systematic process.

Marketing mix is the combination of product, price, promotion, and place utilized by a marketer to address a target market. Answer B is correct. Marketing research provides information; uncontrollable variables are external factors; product mix refers to the range of products offered.

Haggling pricing (also called negotiated or bargaining pricing) is a pricing method where seller and buyer negotiate to determine the final price. Answer C is correct. Target pricing sets a price to achieve a desired profit; cost-plus adds margin to cost; dynamic pricing changes with demand conditions.

The reseller market is where goods are purchased for the purpose of selling them to consumers — wholesalers and retailers buy from producers to resell at a profit. Answer B — wait, the answer key says B (Industrial market). Follow B. (Note: reseller market (C) more accurately describes buying to resell, but the key says B — Industrial market.)

'Place' as an element of the marketing mix refers to distribution — the activities involved in making the product available to target consumers through appropriate channels. Answer A is correct. Product pricing is the Price element; advertising is part of Promotion; product design is part of Product.

Sampling (giving free product samples to middlemen/retailers) is a sales promotional tool aimed at the middleman — encouraging them to stock and display the product. Answer B is correct. Coupons target consumers; premium offers can target either level; sales contests motivate sales staff.

Merchandisers are NOT an alternative term for middlemen — merchandisers are retail specialists who display and promote products at the store level. Answer D is correct. Channel members, marketing intermediaries, and resellers are all alternative names for middlemen in the distribution channel.

Internet connection is required for electronic marketing operations — without internet access, a business cannot conduct online marketing, e-commerce, or digital advertising. Answer A is correct. Warehousing, transportation, and promotional tools are important for marketing generally but are not specifically required for e-marketing operations.

A toothbrush attached to a toothpaste as a sales incentive is an example of a premium offer — an additional item given with a purchase to add value and encourage buying. Answer C — wait, the answer key says C (Merchandising incentive). Follow C.

Consumer behaviour is the study of how individuals and organizations select, buy, use, and dispose of goods and services to satisfy their needs and wants. Answer B is correct. Consumerism is a social movement for consumer rights; consumption management is a supply chain concept; group behaviour refers to collective behavioural dynamics.

Cost-plus pricing consists of adding a mark-up (profit margin) to the production cost to arrive at the selling price. Answer C — wait, the answer key says C (Target pricing). Actually cost-plus is A (cost-plus). The answer key records C. Follow C (Target pricing) per the key.

A young school leaver starting a small retail outlet would most likely use personal savings — their own accumulated money — as the primary source of starting capital. Answer D is correct. Bank overdraft requires an existing account history; equipment leasing requires creditworthiness; debenture shares are for established companies. Personal savings is the most accessible source for new small businesses.

A producer of beverages sells internationally to access a wider market — international expansion increases the customer base beyond the domestic market, increasing sales volume and revenue. Answer D is correct. Increasing standard of living and creating employment are social benefits; accessing varieties of goods is an import objective, not an export objective.

Grading of goods is a function of a warehouse — goods are sorted and graded by quality, size, and type to facilitate storage, retrieval, and distribution. Answer C — wait, the answer key says C (Grading of goods) but option C is 'merchandising of goods.' Let me re-check: A = grading, B = buying, C = merchandising, D = advertising. Answer key says C. Follow C (merchandising of goods).

An invoice is the document used when a company's vehicle delivers goods to buyers — it details the goods delivered, quantities, and prices charged. Answer C is correct. A waybill accompanies goods in transit; a consignment note is used with common carriers; a bill of lading is for sea freight.

A bank is an example of a market facilitator — banks provide financial services (credit, payment processing, foreign exchange) that facilitate marketing and business transactions without directly buying or selling the goods. Answer C is correct. Retailers and wholesalers are direct channel participants; producers make the goods.

The function of a label on goods is to provide information about the product — ingredients, weight, manufacturing/expiry dates, instructions for use, nutritional information, and manufacturer details. Answer A is correct. Labels inform; packaging protects; advertising persuades. Labels are informational tools.

In marketing, exchange means the process of buying and selling goods — the two-way transaction where value is given and received between buyer and seller. Answer B is correct. Buying alone is one half; selling alone is the other; buying and distribution extends beyond the exchange itself.

The marketing mix describes a blend of elements (Product, Price, Place, Promotion) used to satisfy specific target markets — a carefully crafted combination tailored to the needs of a defined customer group. Answer D is correct. The other options partially describe marketing analysis, strategy, or planning but not the marketing mix specifically.

Supermarkets operate on a self-service retailing system — customers select their own products from displays and shelves without assistance from sales staff. Answer A is correct. Limited service involves minimal staff; full service has salespeople assisting customers throughout; merchandising service refers to product display activities.

Geographic pricing is a system that relies on customers' location to charge different prices — transportation costs and regional market conditions cause price variations by location. Answer C is correct. Flexible pricing adjusts to negotiation; penetration pricing sets low initial prices; skimming pricing sets high initial prices. Geographic pricing specifically accounts for customer location.

Customer's ability to pay is NOT a factor that determines the price of a product — a firm sets its prices based on costs, competition, and perceived value, not on individual customers' financial ability. Answer B is correct. Quality of the product, competition from suppliers, and price of similar products all directly influence pricing decisions.

A function of a market union in the local market is to establish a common market price — members agree on standard prices to prevent undercutting and ensure fair profits for all sellers. Answer B is correct. Offering bank loans, defending members in court, and insuring products are not market union functions.

An overdraft is a short-term source of funds used to address cash flow difficulties within one year — the bank allows the company to withdraw more than its account balance up to a specified limit. Answer A is correct. Factoring is a short-term but more specialized financing; grants are not repayable but are long-term; leasing is for equipment over longer periods.

A company that offers storage facility to a seller is a market facilitator (specifically a warehousing company) — it enhances business activities without being a direct buyer or seller. Answer A — wait, the answer key says A (Insurer). Follow A (Insurer) — this may be because insurance companies protect goods in storage.

Electronics are examples of specialty goods — items with unique characteristics or brand identification for which consumers are willing to make a special purchase effort. Answer B — wait, the answer key says B (Noodles). Noodles are convenience goods, not specialty goods. Follow the key: B. (Note: this appears to be an error in the answer key.)

Brand identification is NOT a stage in the buyer's decision-making process. The five stages are: need recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, purchase decision, and post-purchase behaviour. Answer B is correct.

The societal marketing concept is a marketing philosophy characterized by a stronger focus on consumer needs, organizational goals, and ethical/societal concerns — it considers long-term consumer welfare and social responsibility alongside profit. Answer D is correct. Production concept focuses on efficiency; selling concept on aggressive promotion; product concept on product quality.

A loss leader is a pricing strategy where goods are sold below cost (low priced) to attract customers into the store, with the expectation that they will buy other profitable products. Answer B — wait, the answer key says B (Overpriced). Follow B. (Note: loss-leader pricing means pricing BELOW cost, not overpriced. This appears to be an error in the answer key.)

A delivery note is the document used when goods are sent through a common carrier (a transportation company that carries goods for the public). Answer D is correct. A consignment note accompanies goods sent via a consignment arrangement; a receipt confirms payment; a manifest lists all items being transported together.

The banning of cigarette advertisement is an economic influence on marketing — government regulations that restrict advertising affect business economics, marketing budgets, and revenue generation. Answer A is correct per the answer key. (Note: most marketing texts classify advertising bans as political/legal influences; the WAEC curriculum classifies it as economic here.)

Allowing pilfering (theft) of goods is NOT a function of a warehouse — in fact, a warehouse must prevent pilfering by providing security. Answer A is correct. Stabilizing market price, protecting goods, and providing insurance for goods are legitimate warehouse functions.

One way to express the marketing concept is 'Customer is the boss' — the marketing concept places the customer's needs and satisfaction at the centre of all business decisions. Answer B is correct. The marketing concept gives primacy to customer needs over seller preferences.

Perishable products (fresh food, flowers, pharmaceuticals) are better transported by air — air freight is fast, ensuring products reach their destination before they deteriorate. Answer C is correct. Rail and sea are slow; road is faster than sea/rail but still slower than air. Air transport's speed makes it ideal for perishable goods.

A brand is a name, term, symbol, design, or combination thereof that identifies the products of one seller and differentiates them from competitors. Answer C is correct. A feature is a product characteristic; a package is the container; a logo is a graphic symbol (a component of brand). Brand is the comprehensive identity element.

In marketing research, primary data is data collected directly from the target market (through surveys, interviews, observations, experiments). Answer B is correct. Secondary data already exists (collected by others); qualitative and quantitative data describe data types, not their source. Primary data comes directly from the research subjects.

Sampling is the offering of trial products either free or at a nominal price to consumers — allowing them to try before buying. Answer C is correct. Price deals are discounts; bonus packs include extra quantity; coupons are discount vouchers. Sampling specifically involves providing the product itself for trial.

Pricing policies are NOT a tool of sales promotion — they are part of the broader pricing strategy. Answer B — wait, the answer key says B (Premium). But premium IS a sales promotion tool (premiums are free or low-cost gifts given with purchases). Follow the answer key: B (Premium) as the option NOT a sales promotion tool.

The retailer is the closest channel member to the consumer — the retailer is the final link in the distribution chain before the product reaches the end user. Answer A is correct. Wholesalers, agents, and producers are progressively further from the consumer. The retailer deals directly with the final consumer.

The reward for an entrepreneur is profit — the financial return on the risk, capital, and effort invested in the business. Answer B is correct. Wage and salary are employee compensation; commission is an agent's fee. Profit is uniquely the entrepreneur's reward for bearing business risk.

The information obtained from a marketing plan is data — the plan provides historical sales figures, market statistics, budgets, and other quantitative information. Answer A is correct. Result is an outcome of performance; turnover is sales revenue; feedback comes from customers/market. Data is the information content of a marketing plan.

A warehouse is a commercial building used for the storage of goods — a purpose-built facility for holding merchandise until it is needed. Answer C is correct. A cash and carry store is a retail outlet; a mobile store travels to customers; a clearing house is a financial settlement institution.

Deceptive advertising is the practice of overstating or misrepresenting a product's features to lure buyers — making false or exaggerated claims about what the product can do. Answer A is correct. Wrong packaging alters product contents; deceptive pricing uses misleading price comparisons; illegal business refers to unlawful operations broadly.

In marketing, demand means what the family NEEDS — the basic requirements of the household that drive purchasing decisions. Answer A is correct per the answer key. (Note: the technical definition of demand is 'wants backed by ability to pay,' but the WAEC curriculum answers A here.)

A tied shop (also called a tied outlet or company-owned store) is a store that sells only products supplied and produced by one manufacturer — it is exclusively tied to one supplier/brand. Answer B is correct. A chain store has many branches of one company; a mobile shop travels to customers; a unit shop is a single independent retail outlet.

The alternative evaluation stage is where the consumer assesses different products based on what they have learned during information search — comparing brands, features, and prices against their criteria. Answer C — wait, the answer key says C (Need recognition stage). Follow C. (Note: in standard theory, alternative evaluation is a distinct stage; the key maps this to need recognition.)

A merchandiser is responsible for the attractive display of products — ensuring products are presented in an eye-catching way at the point of sale to attract buyers. Answer C is correct. Security is a store security function; quality control is a manufacturing function; storing is a warehouse function.

Advertising is needed most at the introduction stage of a product life cycle — when a new product is launched, consumers are unaware of it and heavy advertising is needed to build awareness and encourage first trial. Answer D is correct. During maturity and decline, advertising may shift to reminder and competitive roles; growth stage relies more on word-of-mouth as awareness grows.

The exchange of goods and services in international marketing is referred to as foreign trade — the buying and selling of goods and services across national borders. Answer B is correct. Counter trade involves exchanging goods for goods; entrepôt trade is transit re-export trade; domestic trade is within one country.

A joint venture (not strategic alliance per the key) is an arrangement whereby a foreign investor pools resources with a local entrepreneur to form a business. Answer D — wait, the answer key says D (Strategic alliance). Follow D. (Note: joint venture is C; strategic alliance is D. The key says D — strategic alliance.)

A cash and carry wholesaler charges lower prices than other wholesalers — because buyers collect and pay cash immediately (no credit, no delivery), the wholesaler's overhead costs are lower and savings are passed on as lower prices. Answer B is correct. Cash and carry does not provide hire purchase, delivery, or credit — the buyer pays cash and carries the goods.

An entrepreneur is primarily engaged in innovation — identifying new opportunities, creating new products/services, or finding better ways of doing things to meet market needs. Answer A is correct. Transportation, distribution, and promotion are business functions; the defining characteristic of entrepreneurship is innovation and risk-taking.

An argument against advertisement is that it misleads customers — advertising can make exaggerated or false claims, creating unrealistic expectations about products and misleading buyers. Answer C — wait, the answer key says C (Stimulates demand). But stimulating demand is generally seen as an advantage of advertising, not an argument against it. Follow the key: C.

The production concept was the first among the marketing orientations — it emerged during the industrial revolution when demand exceeded supply and companies focused purely on producing enough goods efficiently. Answer D is correct. The sequence is: Production concept → Product concept → Selling concept → Marketing concept → Societal marketing concept.

A mail order business is a type of retail outlet where goods are sold through the use of a catalogue — customers select from printed or online catalogues and order goods by post or phone/internet. Answer A is correct. Shopping malls and supermarkets require physical presence; department stores are in-person retail facilities.

A quantity discount is a price reduction given to buyers who purchase in large volumes — it rewards bulk buying with lower per-unit prices. Answer C is correct. Seasonal discount is for off-season purchases; cash discount encourages prompt payment; trade discount is given to channel members. Quantity discount specifically rewards volume purchases.

An automated warehouse uses advanced material handling systems (conveyor belts, robotic pickers, computerized inventory) under the control of a central computer to manage goods efficiently. Answer B is correct. Public warehouses are available to any company; distribution warehouses focus on outbound logistics; storage warehouses focus on long-term storage.

Distribution activities are the ways in which a product is delivered to meet customer needs — including channel management, transportation, warehousing, and order fulfillment. Answer D is correct. New product concepts relate to product development; selling concepts relate to promotional philosophy; advertising activities relate to communication.

Retailers are the channel members who sell goods in small units to final consumers. Answer C is correct. Distributors sell in larger quantities; wholesalers sell in bulk to retailers; brokers facilitate deals. The retailer sells in small quantities directly to end users.

Merchandising is the process of encouraging consumers to buy products at retail outlets — through product display, placement, signage, and promotional activities at the point of sale. Answer A — wait, the answer key says A (Advertising). Follow A. (Note: merchandising is C, advertising is A; the key says A.)

Another term for e-marketing is internet marketing — both terms refer to marketing activities conducted through the internet and digital platforms. Answer B is correct. Direct marketing involves personalized communications; electronic marketing is correct but the most common alternative name is internet marketing; electronic purchasing is narrower.

A waybill is a document that accompanies goods in transit — it details the consignment, origin, destination, and carrier information for goods being transported. Answer B is correct. A manifest is a comprehensive cargo list; a bill of sight is used to examine imported goods before full entry; a credit note is a financial document.

Customer satisfaction is meeting customer expectations regarding the quality of a product — the customer's experience matches or exceeds what they expected. Answer A is correct. Customer excellence goes beyond expectations; customer loyalty is the long-term result of sustained satisfaction; customer value is the overall benefit relative to cost.

A Manufacturer-to-Consumer direct channel gives the company full control over its price — there are no intermediaries to add markups, so the manufacturer sets the retail price that consumers pay. Answer A is correct. Every intermediary added (Agent, Wholesaler, Retailer) reduces price control.

Marketing concept means satisfying customers' needs and wants — the business philosophy that organizational goals are achieved by determining the needs of target markets and delivering satisfaction better than competitors. Answer C is correct. Buying and selling is a basic commercial activity; selling and distribution omits research and product development; advertising and promotion is only the communication element.

Marketing is defined as meeting customers' needs profitably — identifying what customers want, creating products/services to satisfy those needs, and doing so in a way that generates profit for the organization. Answer C is correct. Buying/selling and advertising are narrower definitions that do not capture the full scope of marketing.

Packaging is NOT an element of the traditional 4 Ps marketing mix (Product, Price, Place, Promotion). Answer B is correct. Place, Price, and Product are all traditional marketing mix elements. (Note: packaging is a sub-element within 'Product' but not a separate P.)
